newsitem.title: RUSSIA: China's Jiang optimistic about Russia trip.
newsitem.headline: China's Jiang optimistic about Russia trip.

text.p: Chinese President Jiang Zemin expects "positive results" from a visit to Russia next week that will set the seal on improved ties between the two giant neighbours, Itar-Tass news agency said on Thursday.
"I am deeply convinced that my trip to Moscow will be crowned with positive results," Tass quoted Jiang as saying in an interview with its correspondent in Beijing.
During his visit, from April 22 to 26, Jiang is due to meet President Boris Yeltsin and other senior officials.

"It will be the first top-level meeting since our two countries established an equal, trusting partnership aimed at strategic cooperation in the 21st century," Jiang said, referring to Yeltsin's visit to Beijing last April.
The two presidents would sign a political document setting out their countries' shared views on global issues, Tass quoted Jiang as saying.

Another highlight of Jiang's visit would be the signing by China, Russia and three Central Asian states -- Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan -- of an agreement reducing military forces along the former Soviet-Chinese border.

"(This agreement) has a far-reaching significance for the strengthening of neighbourly relations and friendship and for building peace and stability in the region of our 7,000 km-long border," Jiang said.
The border pact will build on an agreement signed last year committing the five countries to a set of confidence-building border measures.
No details about the timing or extent of planned troop reductions have been announced. China's ambassador to Moscow has said the terms may be kept secret even after the pact is signed.
Russia and China formed a strong alliance in the early 1950s but it degenerated into bitter rivalry for leadership of the communist world and led to border clashes in the late 1960s.

Relations have been warming since Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev visited Beijing in 1989. Visits to China by Yeltsin in December 1992 and in April last year continued the improvement in ties and Jiang has hailed a new era in bilateral relations.
Russian Defence Minister Igor Rodionov is currently on a trip to Beijing to discuss the regional military situation and to promote Russian arms sales to China.
The warming ties contrast with the differenes that have emerged between Russia and the West over NATO's plans to expand eastwards to take in new members for the former Soviet bloc.
